about: Fictional example: a former operations manager who wants a stable, local business with a team in place, and would rather not be the only person who knows how things work.

rates.note: Rough US SBA 7(a) assumptions, not advice. Check current figures before trusting the math.
rates.primeSource: FRED series DPRIME (bank prime loan rate)
rates.sbaTiersSource: SBA.gov, 7(a) terms and conditions: maximum spreads for variable-rate loans by loan amount

manual.label: Food service
manual.explain: Any business that needs licensing for fresh or unpackaged food. A shop selling only packaged goods passes.
manual.digestRule: Restaurants, cafes, bakeries, food trucks, caterers, and shops with a deli or hot-food counter.

manual.label: Outside my region
manual.explain: Outside Example State. A remote business you can run from home passes.
manual.digestRule: Gate only when the operation physically sits outside Example State and needs presence there.

manual.label: The owner is the product
manual.explain: Nothing transferable: a personal brand, an artist's own work, a solo practitioner's practice.
manual.digestRule: Solo practitioner or personal-brand businesses with no other providers.

manual.label: Franchise resale
manual.explain: You'd be buying into a franchisor's rules, fees and approval process.
manual.brokerQ: Franchise fees and royalties, years left on the agreement, and the franchisor's transfer requirements?
manual.digestRule: Listings described as a franchise resale. Franchise ads in alert emails are not listings.

manual.label: Car washes
manual.explain: Fictional example of a personal screen-out: this searcher has decided against car washes.
manual.digestRule: Any listing whose main business is a car wash.

criteriaNote: Each entry refers to the criteria library by id. Add 'name', 'hint', 'anchors' or 'brokerQ' to override the library text, or give a new id with all fields to add a custom judgment criterion. Up and down weights each sum to 100.

geo.homeBaseNote: Used only by Claude for drive-time estimates. Stays in your database; never commit it.

joy.question: How interesting or passionate am I, or could I be, about this business?

anchors.1: Dull or mildly icky. I'd be counting the days.
anchors.2: Meh. The money is the only interesting part.
anchors.3: Pleasant. I'd happily explain it at a party.
anchors.4: Genuinely interesting: next to things I like, or a people-and-process puzzle that hooks me.
anchors.5: I'd be excited to tell people I own it (for this example searcher: bike shops, print shops, maker spaces).

lien.note: Rough US SBA 7(a) assumption, not advice: when business assets don't cover the loan, lenders generally take a lien on personal real estate for the gap. The haircuts are guesses; ask a lender.

perks: Owned brand, IP or online presence
dings: Old or slow inventory sold on top

digest.gmailQuery: label:business-listings OR from:(bizbuysell.com OR bizquest.com OR acquire.com)
digest.topTierPreferences: Stable, recurring revenue; low seasonality; a team in place; within about 50 minutes of home unless it runs without the owner.
